name: 1 in 8 billion
tagline: A browser life sim where an LLM generates a new simulated human life, chapter by chapter, branching on the choices you make.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core loop here is a prompt, a state blob, and three buttons: generate a chapter, offer choices, fold the choice back into the state, repeat. That is close to the canonical demo an AI coding agent builds in an afternoon, and nothing about it needs a server you do not own. What the paid version actually sells is taste: the chapter pacing, the random birth lottery tables, the restraint that keeps the model from writing a Wikipedia summary of a stranger's life. You will rebuild the mechanic quickly and then spend the real time tuning prose quality, which is the part that is not code. Verdict is yes on the build, with the honest caveat that your first version will read like a competent model narrating a spreadsheet.
coreLoopDIY: Rolls a random birth (country, era, family, body, luck) from weighted tables, then has an LLM write successive life chapters that each end in two or three choices which mutate a persistent life state.
requirements: An LLM API key with a few dollars of credit
Willingness to iterate on the system prompt for an hour before the prose stops being generic
whatYouLose: Hand-tuned prompts and narrative pacing that took someone many playthroughs to find
Curated demographic tables, so your random births will skew toward whatever the model thinks is interesting
Illustration, sound, typography and the general feeling of a finished thing
Sharable permalinks and whatever light social layer exists around comparing lives
Someone else absorbing the token bill
moatNotes: The 'proprietary data' is really just a tuned prompt library and weighted life tables, which is a moat for about six weeks and then it is a blog post.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because paying a few dollars for a polished toy beats spending an evening wiring up an API key to get worse prose. The product is a vibe, and vibes are hard to self-host on the first pass: the generated chapters either land or they do not, and the hosted version has already lost the arguments with the model that you are about to have. For most people the honest calculus is that it is cheap entertainment, not infrastructure.
notes: The rare entry where the product and the clone are made of the same material, so the only differentiator left is editorial taste.
prompt:
Build a local single player AI life simulator web app called Lifespan.
Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, and the Anthropic Messages API through the official SDK. No auth, no cloud, no analytics, no telemetry.
Put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.local and read it server side only. Never ship the key to the browser.

Core mechanic:
1. On 'Begin a life', roll a birth from weighted JSON tables in /data: country (weighted by real-ish population share), decade of birth, household income band, family structure, health roll, and one 'quirk'. Seed the RNG from a random string and store the seed so a life can be replayed exactly.
2. Persist a LifeState object: age, location, relationships array, traits array, resources (money, health, reputation as plain integers), and a compact history of prior chapter summaries.
3. Chapter generation: send LifeState plus a strict system prompt to Claude and require a JSON response with { title, prose, ageAfter, stateDelta, choices: [ { label, hint } ] } where prose is 150 to 300 words in close third person and there are exactly 2 or 3 choices.
4. Rendering the choice applies stateDelta, appends a one sentence summary to history, increments age, and generates the next chapter. Life ends on death condition (health at or below 0, or age roll exceeded) with a closing obituary chapter.

Rules for the system prompt: no moralizing, no 'little did she know', no summarizing the whole life early, concrete sensory detail, and the chapter must honor stateDelta rather than contradicting it. Put the prompt in /prompts/chapter.md so it can be edited without touching code.

Also build: a run list page showing past lives with seed, age at death and a one line epitaph; a 'replay this seed' button; and an export to Markdown button.

Out of scope, do not build: accounts, payments, multiplayer, images, sound, mobile apps, leaderboards.
Ship a README with setup steps, the token cost per chapter, and a single `npm run dev` path that works in an empty folder.
